questioned.title: gtkx codegen writes the generated store where gtkx build and gtkx dev cannot resolve it when @gtkx packages are hoisted
questioned.rootCause: resolveStore in packages/codegen/src/store/resolve-store.ts contradicted itself: resolvePackage walked the full node_modules ancestor chain to locate @gtkx/runtime and @gtkx/react and used that hit to version the stores, but resolveStore then discarded the location and anchored both the store directory and its @gtkx symlinks at join(projectRoot, "node_modules"). With npm or yarn workspace hoisting, the app package owns no node_modules, so codegen wrote a complete store into a directory strictly below every package that imports @gtkx/gi and @gtkx/jsx. Vite could not resolve the generated specifiers from the app source, so gtkx:undeclared-library reported the already declared libraries as undeclared, and @gtkx/cli's dev/runner-deps top-level "import * as Gio from \"@gtkx/gi/gio\"" threw ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. pnpm hid the defect because its node_modules/@gtkx/* links realpath back through the project's own node_modules, so the upward walk still crossed the store.
questioned.reviewAssessment:
The change fixes the reported defect at its cause, not at the symptom. `resolvePackage` now records the `node_modules` directory each package was found in during the ancestor walk (captured before `realpathSync`, so a pnpm link directory is used rather than a `.pnpm/` target), and `resolveStore` anchors `gi` at `@gtkx/runtime`'s directory and `jsx` at `@gtkx/react`'s instead of hardcoding `join(projectRoot, "node_modules")`. That is the one line the defect record identified (`resolve-store.ts:91`).

Verified end to end, not just at unit level. I built my own hoisted layout at /tmp/claude-1001/-home-eugenio-gtkx/e764a39a-058a-4899-a510-52f5d1528812/scratchpad/review-hoisted/ws (app at `packages/app`, every @gtkx package and react only in the root `node_modules`) and ran the worktree CLI source: `gtkx codegen` exits 0 and writes `ws/node_modules/.gtkx/{gi,jsx}` with `ws/node_modules/@gtkx/{gi,jsx}` links beside the packages, leaving `packages/app/node_modules` holding only the schema `env.d.ts`; `gtkx build` then exits 0 (221 modules, 7.0 MB bundle) where the same layout previously produced the five `gtkx:undeclared-library` errors.

The regression tests do fail without the change. Rather than checking out the parent into the tree, I extracted `git show 3b838b31^:packages/codegen/src/store/resolve-store.ts` into the scratchpad and drove it with the same fixtures (/tmp/claude-1001/.../scratchpad/oldcheck/driver.ts): the hoisting test yields `<ws>/packages/app/node_modules/.gtkx/gi` where the test asserts `<ws>/node_modules/.gtkx/gi`, and the symlink test fails identically. The third new case ("prefers the nearest node_modules over the hoisted one") passes both before and after, so it is a guard, not a failing-first test. The CLI-side hoisting test fails pre-change for the same reason. Current state: `--project codegen` 550 passed, `--project cli` 430 passed, `typecheck` for both packages successful, `npx eslint` on all three changed source files exits 0.

Callers: every consumer reads the resolved anchor rather than recomputing it. `resolveCodegenStore` forwards the paths; `freshness.ts`, `codegenOptions`, and `clearGeneratedStores` all consume `CodegenStore`; `commands/docs.ts` uses `resolveStore(cwd).gi.storeDir`, which now points where codegen wrote. `settings/schema.ts` and `create-gtkx/scaffolder.ts` keep writing `env.d.ts` under the project's own `node_modules/.gtkx`, which stays correct because the scaffolded `src/gtkx-env.d.ts` references that project-local path and the file carries schema declarations, not store types. No monorepo package moves: `packages/{components,e2e,testing}` and `examples/gtk-demo` each own `node_modules/@gtkx/runtime`, so the walk stops at the same directory as before, and `examples/{browser,hello-world}` are `codegen: false`.

Conventions: no inline exports, section order preserved (imports, types, constants, functions, exports), only JSDoc added, no `!`, no `as unknown as`, no `readonly`, lines within 120 columns, no em dashes in the guide sentence. No legacy path, shim, or dual-support branch was left; the `packages/<name>` monorepo fallback still reports `projectRoot/node_modules` and is still reachable.
reviewProblems: Split anchor between the two stores. `gi` is anchored at @gtkx/runtime's node_modules while `jsx` is anchored at @gtkx/react's, and the generated `@gtkx/jsx` peer-depends on and imports `@gtkx/gi` (node_modules/.gtkx/jsx/package.json peerDependencies, and jsx/gtk/gtk.js imports "@gtkx/gi/gtk"). When react resolves from a shallower node_modules than runtime, jsx lands above gi and cannot resolve it, which is the original ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND class again. Demonstrated against the current source in /tmp/claude-1001/-home-eugenio-gtkx/e764a39a-058a-4899-a510-52f5d1528812/scratchpad/oldcheck/split.ts (react at <ws>/node_modules, runtime at <ws>/packages/app/node_modules): gi storeDir = <ws>/packages/app/node_modules/.gtkx/gi, jsx storeDir = <ws>/node_modules/.gtkx/jsx. Hardening is one line: anchor jsx at the gi anchor (or at whichever of the two is shallower), since gi must always be at or above jsx.

codegen can now write outside the project root with no bound and no error path. `nodeModulesChain` walks to the filesystem root, so a project directory nested under any unrelated GTKX install now has its store written into that install's node_modules, and `swapStore` replaces the existing store there (renaming it to `.old`). Before the change the write always stayed inside the project. Fingerprint freshness makes the two projects regenerate over each other rather than corrupt permanently, but `gtkx codegen` mutating another project's node_modules, or failing with EACCES when the ancestor directory is read-only (a common container layout), is new behavior. The defect record accepted a loud failure as the alternative outcome; neither a guard nor a diagnostic exists.

The two store-removal paths now disagree. `clearGeneratedStores` (packages/cli/src/codegen/run-codegen.ts:105) deletes the anchored store, while `removeSharedStoreShadow` (line 61) still hardcodes `resolve(cwd, "node_modules/...")`. In a hoisted layout the store a project generated sits at the workspace root, so switching that project to `codegen: false` removes nothing and it keeps consuming its own generated store, contradicting website/guide/configuration-and-codegen.md:33 ("skips generation, so the project imports whatever binding store is already installed").

The diagnostic half of the defect entry is untouched. The entry's oracle is Oracle 1 compounded by Oracle 8, and `undeclaredLibraryError` in packages/cli/src/vite-plugins/undeclared-library.ts:28 still branches only on whether GIR data exists, never on whether the store on disk already holds the namespace. It no longer fires for this repro, but any other unresolvable-store situation (the split anchor above, a failed or read-only store write) still tells the user to add a library that is already declared.

questioned.title: Writing a field through a struct-valued field getter is silently discarded, the getter returns a detached copy
questioned.rootCause: A struct field whose type is embedded inline in its owner was decoded through the pointer-slot path of its codec. `read_inlineable_pointer_slot!` (packages/native/src/ffi/codec/prelude.rs) consumed the descriptor's `inline` flag only to skip the dereference, then forwarded the interior pointer to `read_value`, which cannot see the flag: `BoxedCodec::read_value` fell through to `copied()` (`g_boxed_copy`) and `StructCodec::read_value` to `borrow_or_copy()` (`g_memdup2`). Either way JavaScript received a handle to a fresh allocation, so `rect.origin.x = 99` wrote into a detached copy and the owner was untouched, while `rect.origin = point` and flat writes such as `rgba.red = 0.5` went through the in-place `write_inline` path and did reach the owner. `api::read` is the only place holding both the owner handle and the field offset, so the aliasing could not be expressed inside the codec at all.
questioned.reviewAssessment:
The change fixes the reported defect at its cause rather than masking the assertions. `api::read` (packages/native/src/api/read.rs:35) now short-circuits on `Codec::is_inline()` and hands back `Handle::field(owner, offset)`, a handle whose `as_ptr()` is `owner.as_ptr() + offset`, so every inline field descriptor in the generated stores decodes to an alias of its owner and the pre-existing in-place `write_inline` path reaches the owner. That covers all 14 `isInline: true` descriptors emitted across the stores (5 `t.boxed`, 9 `t.struct`; no fundamental ones), not just the two the test exercises, and it is the only decode path a field descriptor can take (`isInline` is emitted only by record-field-accessor.ts and record-constructor.ts).

The regression test does fail without the change. Graphene's `origin` is `t.boxed("GraphenePoint", {ownership:"borrowed", getTypeFnName:"graphene_point_get_type", isInline:true, size:8})` — no `freeFnName`, not caller-allocated — so the parent's `BoxedCodec::read_value` fell to `copied()` (`g_boxed_copy`); Pango's `geometry` is `t.struct("borrowed",{size:12,isInline:true})`, so `StructCodec::read_value` fell to `borrow_or_copy()` (`g_memdup2`, size known). Both handed JavaScript a detached allocation, which is what the record replayed 10/10. The three round-trip assertions cannot pass against that code. The other two cases in the file are guards for hazards the alias introduces (self-assignment, wholesale replacement), and they pass either way by design.

Nothing else breaks. I ran, on the fix commit: the full e2e project (131 files, 1329/1329), runtime+components+testing (60 files, 750/750), the entire native cargo suite under the headless compositor (all binaries, 0 failures, no warnings), `struct_codec` + `ownership_matrix` under AddressSanitizer with leak detection, `pnpm typecheck` (exit 0), `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` (clean), `cargo fmt --check` (clean), and eslint on the new test (clean). I also traced every consumer of what changed: `field_store()`'s new tuple return has one production caller (api/write.rs, which now keys adoption by the absolute offset in the root struct, correct for both a root Struct handle, base 0, and a nested alias); `Handle`'s move behind `Rc` touches `take_owned`/`as_ptr`/`size_hint`/`invalidate` callers only mechanically; `Handle::field` over a Boxed/Borrowed owner returns `None` from `field_store`, matching the previous behavior for those owners. The deleted `read_inlineable_pointer_slot!` macro leaves no residue (no references remain), and the codecs' fallback to the default `Decoder::read_pointer_slot` is byte-identical for the non-inline case. The struct-array accessors (`renderStructArrayAccessor`) are untouched: they use a non-inline `t.struct` and write the modified copy back through the pointer slot, which is why the Pango glyph round-trip still holds.

Conventions: no inline exports, section order correct (imports, function, side effect), no comments, no `!`, no `as unknown as`, no `readonly` in the new TypeScript; the Rust doc comments match the surrounding style. No legacy path, shim, or dead branch is left alive; the two ownership-matrix cells and `an_inline_field_is_read_at_its_own_address` were corrected to assert the new contract (pointer identity against the owner's field address) rather than relaxed, and a keep-alive case was added.

On a narrower fix: the alternative is to keep the copy and stop codegen emitting the nested setter, which the record allowed but which removes capability. Holding the owner through a napi `Ref` instead of `Rc` would confine the cost to field handles; as written, every handle pays one extra heap allocation and refcount, on the path taken for every decoded GObject, and no benchmark was run.
reviewProblems: Residual risk, not current breakage: the `inline` flag is now honored in exactly one place (api/read.rs:35). `Decoder::read_pointer_slot` no longer special-cases it, so an inline codec reached through a Slot source dereferences the field's own bytes as a pointer, with no assert and no bail to catch it. That is precisely the AddressSanitizer SEGV the fixer hit mid-work on the ownership matrix. I verified no production caller does this today (the only Slot reads are api::read, which is guarded, plus ref.rs inner codecs and closure.rs callback args, neither of which ever carries a field descriptor), but a future descriptor with isInline reaching a slot read crashes instead of copying.

Lifetime semantics change for owners GTKX does not own. The `Rc` keeps the owner *handle* alive, not the underlying allocation, so `HandleKind::Borrowed` owners gain a use-after-free window: `const o = transientRect.origin` held past the C memory's validity now reads freed bytes, where the old copy was self-contained. This follows from the requested behavior, but no test covers a borrowed owner outliving a field handle, while the owned-struct case does have one.

The inline branch drops the null guard. The old path went through `decode_non_null`, which returns JavaScript `null` for a null pointer; the new branch builds a handle at address `offset` regardless. `live_handle_ptr` only rejects invalidated Object handles, so a Struct/Boxed/Borrowed handle carrying null would now produce a wrapper over a bogus address. Not reachable through the generated stores (decode paths yield JS null rather than null-pointer handles, and `alloc` never returns null), so it is latent only.

`#[must_use]` was added to `Handle::take_owned`, which mutates (it takes the value out of a Cell). Existing callers write `drop(handle.take_owned())` so nothing breaks, but the attribute states the opposite of what the function does; it was added to silence `clippy::must_use_candidate` after the `Rc` change rather than because the result must be used.

Adoption still stops at a Boxed or Borrowed root: `field_store()` returns None for those kinds, so an owned pointer written into a nested inline field of, say, a Graphene.Rect is never adopted and leaks (`PendingTransfer` has no Drop). This is pre-existing for boxed owners and unchanged by the commit, but the new nested-write capability makes the hole reachable through one more route than before.
